recommendations.regimenLabel: Pattern-specific therapy — immunosuppression for inflammatory ILD, antifibrotics for IPF (specialist-directed)
steps: HRCT chest and full PFTs; refer respiratory ILD service / MDT.
Identify cause — drugs, connective-tissue disease, occupational/environmental, hypersensitivity.
Treatment is pattern-specific: immunosuppression for inflammatory ILD; antifibrotics (pirfenidone/nintedanib) for IPF.
Oxygen for hypoxaemia; pulmonary rehabilitation; vaccinations.
Manage comorbidities; consider transplant referral in advanced disease.

drugRefs.dose: ~0.5 mg/kg/day, then taper to lowest effective dose (specialist-directed)
drugRefs.why: For inflammatory (non-IPF) ILD such as connective-tissue-disease-associated or hypersensitivity pneumonitis. Not indicated in and can be harmful in IPF.

drugRefs.dose: titrate to 801 mg three times daily (2403 mg/day)
drugRefs.why: Slows FVC decline in idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis. Monitor LFTs; photosensitivity precautions.
Slows lung-function decline in IPF and other progressive fibrosing ILDs. Monitor LFTs; diarrhoea is common.

refs: Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine, 22e — Interstitial Lung Diseases
ATS/ERS/JRS/ALAT Clinical Practice Guideline — Idiopathic Pulmonary Fibrosis: Diagnosis and Treatment

confirm: Progressive exertional dyspnoea, dry cough, fine bibasal 'velcro' crackles; restrictive spirometry; HRCT pattern.
